title: CS6910: Lecture 2
description: ## **Lecture 2:** McCulloch Pitts Neuron, Thresholding Logic, Perceptrons, Perceptron Learning Algorithm and Convergence, Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs), Representation Power of MLPs. ### At the end of this lecture, student will have a good understanding of the following topics:. * ### Perceptron Learning Algorithm and Convergence. ### **Module 2.1: Biological Neurons**. ### The most fundamental unit of a deep neural network is called an**artificial** *neuron*. ### Why is it called a neuron ? ### Of course, in reality, it is not just a single neuron which does all this. ### Some of these neurons may fire (in red) in response to this information and in turn relay information to other neurons they are connected to. g(x\_1,x\_2,...,x\_n) = g(x) = \sum\_{i=1}^{n}\ x\_i. ### In other words, all inputs which produce an output 0 will be on one side \((\sum\_{i=1}^{n}\ x\_i<\theta\)) of the line and all inputs which produce an output 1 will lie on the other side \((\sum\_{i=1}^{n}\ x\_i\geq \theta\)) of this line.
